title: Common layout patterns and debugging
learningObjectives: Explain common layout patterns and debugging and build a responsive layout with it.

understand.concept: Flexbox supports common patterns such as navigation bars, button groups, media objects, card footers, and centered content. Debugging involves checking the container's direction, wrapping, available size, item basis, minimum sizes, gaps, and alignment.
understand.whyItMatters: A layout can fail because an item cannot shrink, a parent has an unexpected width, or the axes are misunderstood. Inspecting the flex overlay and computed properties is faster than adding random margins.
understand.analogy: A layout pattern is a reusable arrangement recipe; debugging means checking each constraint that influences how the items share space.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual layout follows the flex or grid formatting algorithm.

practise.independentTask: Build a small responsive interface using the concept. Test long labels and more than one viewport width.

questions.prompt: What should you inspect first when a flex item unexpectedly overflows?
options: Its container size, item sizing, and minimum-size constraints
questions.answer: Its container size, item sizing, and minimum-size constraints
questions.explanation: Flex overflow commonly relates to available space, basis, and automatic minimum sizing.

questions.prompt: What is a good way to debug a flex or grid layout?
options: Inspect the container and item sizing in developer tools
Add random margins until the layout looks right
questions.answer: Inspect the container and item sizing in developer tools
questions.explanation: Inspecting track or flex sizing and computed properties identifies the real constraint.
